metadata.title: Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) Platform SSPP
metadata.remarks: System Security and Privacy Plan governing the institutional Public Key Infrastructure, establishing authoritative cryptographic trust, certificate lifecycle governance, and revocation enforcement.

import-profile.remarks: Institutional security and privacy baseline profile.

system-characteristics.system-description: The PKI Platform provides centralized issuance, validation, and revocation of digital certificates for institutional identities, systems, and services, enabling cryptographically verifiable trust at scale.

props.name: platform-role
props.remarks: Public Key Infrastructure is a Tier-1 institutional platform underpinning identity, secure communication, and cryptographic trust for all services.

props.name: implements-pattern
props.remarks: This SSPP is the authoritative implementation and assurance anchor for the Public Key Infrastructure security pattern.

props.name: depends-on-sspp
props.remarks: PKI relies on the Key Management Platform for secure generation, protection, rotation, and destruction of asymmetric keys.

props.name: depends-on-sspp
props.remarks: Certificate issuance and binding rely on Secure Identity for identity proofing and authorization.

props.name: depends-on-sspp
props.remarks: PKI services rely on Secure Network for protected communication and monitoring.

props.name: cryptographic-compliance
props.remarks: All cryptographic modules supporting certificate issuance, signing, storage, and validation must be FIPS 140-3 validated.

props.name: ca-key-protection
props.remarks: Root and subordinate Certificate Authority private keys must be generated, stored, and operated within HSMs.

props.name: device-identity-model
props.remarks: Device and server identity certificates must be backed by TPM-protected private keys where supported.

props.name: certificate-issuance-model
props.remarks: All institutional certificates must be issued through the PKI Platform; application-managed or self-signed certificates are prohibited unless explicitly exempted.

props.name: revocation-enforcement
props.remarks: Certificate revocation checking (OCSP and/or CRL) is mandatory for all trust decisions; revocation bypass is prohibited.

props.name: certificate-lifespan
props.remarks: Certificates should be short-lived where technically feasible to limit blast radius and simplify revocation.

system-implementation.remarks: The PKI Platform enforces institutionally controlled certificate issuance, validation, and revocation for users, devices, services, and infrastructure.

roles.title: Certificate Authority Operator
roles.remarks: Operates root and intermediate certificate authorities, including ceremonies, issuance, and revocation.

roles.title: PKI Architecture Authority
roles.remarks: Defines certificate policies, trust models, lifetimes, and acceptable cryptographic profiles.

roles.title: PKI Operations
roles.remarks: Manages certificate services, revocation infrastructure, and trust validation services.

control-implementation.remarks: All certificate issuance, validation, and revocation controls are enforced by the PKI Platform and inherited by applications and services. Applications are prohibited from acting as certificate authorities or from bypassing PKI validation.
